rem:non-self-intersection-interpretation: Remark Quantum exclusion zone and the Pauli analogue. Physically, the R-matrix endows the vortex filament \varrho with a "quantum exclusion zone" of radius \hbar_q. The filament cannot pass through itself because doing so would demand infinite categorical energy. This constitutes the knot-theoretic analogue of the Pauli exclusion principle, with the non-cocommutativity of \Delta_q serving as fermionic statistics.
sec:crossing-energy-intro: Localizing the global Möbius self-avoidance kernel at the crossings of a braid projection decomposes the crossing energy E_\times (Definition) into a symmetric strong baseline and an orientation-odd electromagnetic shift proportional to the Coulomb charge Q(\mathfrak{H}) = \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-) (Definition). This section develops these crossing-energy identities on the trefoil and in the commutative limit over the categorical coordinate ring R[i, q^{\pm 1}].
rem:crossing-energy-categorical-origin:
Remark Crossing weights are Hecke eigenvalues, not postulates. The per-crossing weights (q, -q^{-1}) of the crossing energy are not an energetic penalty laid on top of a topological framework. They are the two eigenvalues of the Hecke generator T = P \circ R \colon V \otimes V \to V \otimes V acting on the symmetric/antisymmetric decomposition. The rigid monoidal structure forces them:

  1. Rigidity fixes the R-matrix determinant. Dualisability of V and the categorical volume constraint (volume constraint) require the braiding R = c_{V,V} to satisfy \det(R|_{V \otimes V}) = 1, with eigenvalues (q, q^{-1}) on S^{2} V \oplus \Lambda^{2} V.
  2. The Hecke generator carries the transposition sign. The Hecke generator is T = P \circ R, where P is the swap. Since P|_{\Lambda^{2} V} = -\mathrm{id}, composition flips the sign on the antisymmetric summand. This gives T-eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}) with \det(T) = -1, which matches the Hecke minimal polynomial (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 (eigenvalue extraction).
  3. Crossing weights are eigenvalues, not postulates. Assigning a positive crossing L_{+} the weight q and a negative crossing L_{-} the weight -q^{-1} represents precisely the action of T on a symmetric-channel input and T^{-1} on an antisymmetric-channel input. The sum \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) is therefore a trace of T^{\pm 1}-eigenvalues along the braid. The categorical structure dictates this assignment.
  4. Gröbner--Shirshov resolution. When \mathfrak{H} is reduced to Gröbner--Shirshov normal form, each crossing contributes its T-eigenvalue exactly once. The net \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} is the resulting Laurent polynomial in q, read off the normal form. Removing any of these weights would violate duality and break the Hecke relation.

Compute this quantity entirely from the R-matrix braiding (R-matrix) of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) acting on the tensor product of constituent representations.
ex:crossing-energy-trefoil:
Example Crossing energy and binding in the trefoil. Evaluate the crossing energy (crossing energy) for the trefoil knot and then detail how binding arises in hadrons.

Single crossing energy. Each crossing in a knot diagram carries Skein weight q (positive crossing) or -q^{-1} (negative crossing). For a positive crossing, the energy contribution is

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}^{(+)} = q,
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}^{(-)} = -q^{-1}.

The net energy of a single positive crossing minus a single negative crossing is q - q^{-1}. This coefficient appears in the Skein relation T - T^{-1} = q - q^{-1}.

Trefoil: three positive crossings. The standard diagram of the trefoil \tau(2,3) has three positive crossings. Its total crossing energy is

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\tau(2,3))
  =  3q.

At the aether parameter q \approx 1.110:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\tau(2,3))
   \approx  3 \times 1.110
  =  3.330.

This is positive. The trefoil is a single knot, not a composite, so there is no linking to provide negative binding energy.

Binding in composites. A hadron \mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L} is a composite. Its linking \mathcal{L} introduces additional crossings between constituent knots. Mutual crossings between distinct components can contribute negative energy (via negative crossings in the linking braid word). The total crossing energy of a composite is

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H})
  = 
  \underbrace{\sum_{i} \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(K_i)}_{\text{self-crossings (positive)}}
  + 
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathcal{L})}_{\text{mutual crossings (can be negative)}}.

The composite is bound when the total is negative: \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) < 0. The mutual linking energy overcomes the individual knot crossing costs. The composite is energetically favorable relative to the separated constituents.

Proton binding. The proton (proton as Borromean hadron) consists of three quarks linked in a Borromean configuration. The Borromean linking contributes enough negative mutual crossing energy to make \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p}) < 0. This explains why the proton is a stable bound state: disassembling it into free quarks demands adding energy equal to |\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p})|.
rem:commutative-crossing-energy:
Remark Categorical coordinate of the commutative limit: i as \sqrt{\lambda_-} and the \mathbb{Z}_2 \hookrightarrow \mathrm{U}(1) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{U}_q(1) hierarchy. The Hecke generator \sigma = P \circ R on V \otimes V has eigenvalues (\lambda_+, \lambda_-) = (q, -q^{-1}) on the symmetric/antisymmetric decomposition S^2 V \oplus \Lambda^2 V (def:crossing-energy). At q = 1 (def:commutative-qou), the eigenvalues collapse to (+1, -1) = \mathbb{Z}_2, and the per-crossing weight q - q^{-1} vanishes identically. The categorical structure of the commutative limit is recovered by extracting the square root of the antisymmetric eigenvalue \lambda_- = -1:

  i  =  \sqrt{\lambda_-}, \qquad i^2 + 1  =  0  \;\text{in}\; R[i].

The categorical structure forces the ring extension R[i] (the universal R-algebra containing an element i with i^2 = -1). The element i is the categorical coordinate of \mathbb{P}(V) in the commutative limit, mirroring the role of q in the non-commutative theory. The construction is intrinsic to R; no real or complex numbers are assumed. When R already contains a square root of -1 (e.g. the archimedean realisation where R = \mathbb{C}, see archimedean realisations), i \in R is canonical. When R does not (e.g. R = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] at q = 1), R[i] is the minimal extension realising \lambda_- as a categorical square.

Categorical-coordinate dictionary.

See Table 1.

Deformation hierarchy. The discrete Weyl group \mathbb{Z}_2 embeds into the continuous maximal torus, which itself is the q = 1 fibre of the quantum torus:

  \mathbb{Z}_2  \;\hookrightarrow\;  \mathrm{U}(1)  \;\hookrightarrow\;
   \mathrm{U}_q(1).

Each inclusion identifies a different categorical coordinate on \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}). The value -1 generates \mathbb{Z}_2; i generates \mathrm{U}(1) at the quarter-turn \varTheta = \pi/2; and q generates \mathrm{U}_q(1) off-locus. The standard non-commutative deformation \mathrm{SU}(2) \rightsquigarrow \mathrm{SU}_q(2) acts on the second inclusion. The commutative-limit enlargement \mathbb{Z}_2 \hookrightarrow \mathrm{U}(1) acts on the first. These are the two mechanisms to escape the q = 1 degeneracy of q - q^{-1}.

Three categorical readings of i on \mathbb{P}(V).

  1. Algebraic. i = \sqrt{\lambda_-} \in \mathrm{End}_{R[i]}(\mathbf{1}) is the categorical square root of the antisymmetric braiding eigenvalue. This single datum appears in three faces: Wick rotation, CR complex structure, and arrow of time. All reduce to the binary choice of braiding orientation c_{V,V} vs c_{V,V}^{-1} (rem:i-as-braiding-orientation).
  2. Geometric. J = i \cdot \mathrm{id}_V \in \mathrm{End}_{R[i]}(V) is an endomorphism with J^2 = -\mathrm{id}_V, descending to a complex structure on \mathbb{P}(V) = \mathrm{Proj}(\mathrm{Sym}\, V^\vee) over R[i]. In the archimedean realisation, this recovers the standard complex structure on the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2 (def:exceptional-divisor).
  3. Equivariant. The maximal torus \mathrm{U}(1) \subset \mathrm{SU}(2) acts on \mathbb{P}(V) with i as the quarter-turn generator. The orbit space is [0, \pi] with phase fibre \varphi \in S^1 over the interior (prop:u1-equivariant-reduction).

The three readings coincide because each computes the same categorical datum: a square root of \lambda_- in \mathrm{End}_{R[i]}(V).

Affine-chart origin. Both q and i originate from the chart-transition data of \mathbb{P}(V) (rem:affine-chart-origin-of-i-and-q). The parameter q constitutes the chart-transition coefficient z\,w = q^{-1} on the quantum projective line \mathbb{P}_q(V). The element i is the square root of the chart-swap involution \iota: z \mapsto z^{-1} that the transition collapses to at q = 1. Formally, the categorical-coordinate ring is the universal R-algebra extension R[i, q^{\pm 1}] = R[q, q^{-1}][i]/(i^2 + 1) (prop:categorical-coordinate-ring) in which q is invertible and the involution-eigenvalue -1 possesses a square root. The chart-transition automorphism group factors as \langle q \rangle \rtimes \langle \iota \rangle over this ring.

Half-twist and ribbon structures. The ribbon element v = q^{1/2} is not required for the categorical-coordinate construction. It appears only when \mathbf{C} carries an additional ribbon twist \varTheta_V = q^{1/2}\,\mathrm{id}_V for framed-link invariants or Reshetikhin--Turaev TQFT (rem:sqrt-q-ribbon-structure). Extract the square root of \lambda_- within R[i], not from any ribbon datum. It remains independent of the eigenvalue-labelling convention q := \lambda_+ (rem:braiding-unit-circle-convention).

Crossing energy in the commutative limit. Setting q = e^{i\varTheta} on the unit circle of \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) gives

  q - q^{-1}  =  2i \sin\varTheta,

with \varTheta \in [0, \pi] tracking the orbit-space interval of prop:u1-equivariant-reduction. The endpoints \varTheta = 0, \pi define the polar fixed points (zero weight). The interior constitutes the free S^1-fibre. The point \varTheta = \pi/2 (where q = i) marks the location of maximum weight |2i \sin(\pi/2)| = 2. The Hecke energy q - q^{-1} of the non-commutative theory operates as the algebraic deformation of this commutative-limit form.

prop:coulomb-strong-ratio-q-rational:
Proposition Coulomb/strong ratio \tanh(\ln q) is the q-rational (q^2-1)/(q^2+1). For every real q > 0 (the aether-anchor regime, \mathrm{Im}(q) = 0 at the archimedean place), the ratio satisfies:

  \tanh(\ln q) \;=\; \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}} \;=\; \frac{q^2 - 1}{q^2 + 1}.

On a positive braid closure the antisymmetric-to-symmetric ratio of the Coulomb charge equals the q-rational expression (q_0^2 - 1)/(q_0^2 + 1) at the aether anchor. The analytic and the algebraic forms are a single object.

Significance

The antisymmetric-to-symmetric ratio equals \tanh(\ln q) on a positive braid closure — that is, at n_- = 0. This proposition confirms that on that locus the analytic and the algebraic forms coincide identically over real q > 0. The identity below is independent of that scoping: it is a statement about \tanh, and holds for every real q > 0 whatever the crossing counts. This removes any ambiguity regarding whether the framework employs a "classical-\tanh" or a "q-deformed \tanh_q" realization at the aether anchor.

The forms match because \exp(\ln q) = q for q > 0. Therefore,

  \tanh(\ln q)
  \;=\; \frac{e^{\ln q} - e^{-\ln q}}{e^{\ln q} + e^{-\ln q}}
  \;=\; \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  \;=\; \frac{q^2 - 1}{q^2 + 1}
  \quad\text{(multiply numerator and denominator by \(q\)).}
prf:coulomb-strong-ratio-q-rational:
Proof Proof of coulomb strong ratio q rational. The proof has two steps:

  1. Algebraic identity: for any real q \ne 0,

      \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}} = \frac{q^2 - 1}{q^2 + 1}.

    Clearing denominators reduces it to a polynomial identity.

  2. Transcendental bridge: for any real q > 0,

      \tanh(\ln q) = \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}.

    Follows from e^{\ln q} = q and the definitions of \sinh, \cosh, \tanh.

The composite (Coulomb/strong ratio \tanh(\ln q) is the q-rational (q^2-1)/(q^2+1)) is the immediate corollary: \tanh(\ln q) = (q^2-1)/(q^2+1) for q > 0.

q-usage discipline

The identity is stated and proved over \mathbb{R}_{>0} (the archimedean aether-anchor regime). The fibre-level q-rational form (q-q^{-1})/(q+q^{-1}) is a Laurent-polynomial ratio over \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}], realised at q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} where it agrees with the archimedean \tanh(\ln q_0). There is no |q| = 1 step (the identity involves q^{-1} algebraically, not as conjugation; both q_0 and q_0^{-1} are real positive points). Compliant with the requirement that q_0 have vanishing imaginary part.
prop:skein-crossing-asymmetry:
Proposition Crossing asymmetry and per-crossing Coulomb correction. The Skein relation assigns positive crossings a weight of q and negative crossings a weight of q^{-1}:

  q  L_+ -  q^{-1} L_-
  =  (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}) L_0.

For q > 1, the per-crossing repulsive Coulomb correction relative to a mixed-charge baseline evaluates to:

  \delta_{\mathrm{Coulomb}}
  =  q -  \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1})
  =  \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})
   >  0.

The ratio of the antisymmetric (Coulomb) to symmetric (strong) Skein weights is:

  \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  =  \tanh(\ln q).

At q = 1, the asymmetry vanishes. As q \to \infty, the ratio approaches 1.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. The generic categorical/q-deformation identities it relies upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
rem:skein-crossing-asymmetry:
Remark Crossing asymmetry and emergent Coulomb repulsion. The R-matrix braiding (R-matrix) enforces a fundamental asymmetry between positive and negative crossings. The Skein relation

  q  L_+ -  q^{-1} L_-
  =  (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}) L_0

weights positive crossings by q and negative crossings by q^{-1}. Because q > 1, positive crossings contribute more to the Skein polynomial than negative ones. This asymmetry constitutes the topological origin of electromagnetic repulsion.

Emergent Coulomb repulsion. For a hadron \mathfrak{H} with Coulomb charge Q(\mathfrak{H}) (Coulomb charge), the crossing energy (crossing energy) decomposes into a symmetric (strong) baseline and an antisymmetric (Coulomb) correction. The per-crossing repulsive correction between composites of the same charge relative to a mixed-charge baseline is

  \delta_{\mathrm{Coulomb}}
  =  q -  \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1})
  =  \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})
  > 0.

Unification of strong and electromagnetic interactions. Electromagnetic repulsion does not operate as a separate force in the QOU framework. It is a phase asymmetry in the same Skein polynomial that dictates the strong binding. Both interactions stem from the R-matrix braiding of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)). The parameter q controls their relative strength:

  • The strong binding scales with \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1}) (the baseline Skein weight).
  • The electromagnetic repulsion scales with \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) (the crossing asymmetry).

Their ratio evaluates to

  \frac{\text{Coulomb}}{\text{Strong}}
  =  \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  =  \tanh\!\left(\ln q\right).

At q = 1 (classical limit), the asymmetry vanishes and the electromagnetic interaction disappears. At q \to \infty (deep-quantum regime), the ratio approaches 1 and the two interactions balance.

Chapter 6 details the specific assignment of Coulomb charges to protons and neutrons, and its consequences for nuclear stability, which require the Descartes universe (\chi = -6).
prop:skein-bar-antisymmetry:
Proposition Skein relation L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0 is bar-antisymmetric. The Hecke--Skein relation

  L_+ - L_-  =  (q - q^{-1})\,L_0
  \tag{S}

in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) is antisymmetric under the bar involution

  \overline{\,\cdot\,} \colon
  (L_+,\,L_-,\,L_0,\,q)
  \;\longmapsto\;
  (L_-,\,L_+,\,L_0,\,q^{-1}).

Applying \overline{\,\cdot\,} to both sides of (S) yields -1 times (S):

  \overline{L_+ - L_-}  =  L_- - L_+
   =  -\,(L_+ - L_-),
  \qquad
  \overline{(q - q^{-1})\,L_0}
   =  (q^{-1} - q)\,L_0
   =  -\,(q - q^{-1})\,L_0.
prf:skein-bar-antisymmetry:
Proof Proof of skein bar antisymmetry. The bar involution swaps L_+ \leftrightarrow L_- and q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} while fixing L_0. Direct substitution gives both equalities above. \square

Corollary (case-split collapse).

Any proof in the braid--knot framework that establishes a property \Phi(L_+) for the positive crossing automatically establishes \Phi(L_-) for the negative crossing, provided \Phi is formulated \overline{\,\cdot\,}-equivariantly (i.e., \Phi(\overline{x}) = \overline{\Phi(x)} on the relevant target). The bar involution transports the proof verbatim.

Wherever the corollary applies — a pair of positive/negative crossing computations, a per-crossing-sign feasibility check, an enumeration of L_+ and L_- contributions to a state sum — the bar-antisymmetry of (S) means those contributions enter the analysis as bar-paired terms, not independent ones. The case-split is pure bookkeeping.

Categorical statement.

The bar involution defines a contravariant functor \overline{\,\cdot\,} \colon H_n(q) \to H_n(q^{-1})^{\mathrm{op}} sending each generator \sigma_i to \sigma_i^{-1} in the opposite algebra. The Skein relation is the assertion that this functor intertwines the two crossing types, with the sign flip in (S) encoding the antisymmetry.
sec:lagrange-q-kinematics-intro: Diagonalizing the cyclic sheet permutation C_5 \subset S_5 on the five branch sheets of Bring's surface via the discrete Fourier transform produces the Lagrange resolvents w_0, \ldots, w_4 (Proposition).
rem:lagrange-resolvents:
Remark Lagrange resolvents and spectral form. Let \zeta=e^{2\pi i/n}. The discrete Fourier transform on C_n (Lagrange resolvent transform) diagonalises the cyclic action: \sigma(w_k) = \zeta^{-k} w_k. Any C_n-invariant polynomial constraint on the coordinates x_j transforms to constraints on C_n-equivariant combinations of the Fourier modes w_k.

For n = 5 (Bring's surface), the three power-sum equations become:

\begin{align}
  w_0 &= 0
    &&\text{(linear projection),}
    \label{eq:resolvent-linear}\\[4pt]
  w_1w_4+w_2w_3 &= 0
    &&\text{(Hermitian quadric),}
    \label{eq:resolvent-quadric}\\[4pt]
  w_1^2w_3+w_4^2w_2+w_2^2w_1+w_3^2w_4 &= 0
    &&\text{(symmetric cubic).}
    \label{eq:resolvent-cubic}
\end{align}

The quadric pairs conjugate modes (w_k with w_{5-k}). The cubic pairs squared modes in the skip-one pattern. These are the C_5-equivariant invariants h_2 and h_3 (aggregate color quantities).
def:q-momentum:
Definition q-Momentum from the braid writhe. Let \beta \in B_n be the canonical braid representative — the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form at the minimal level of the brane tower — of a particle knot K = \hat{\beta} (braid closure), with generators \sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_k}^{\epsilon_k} where \epsilon_j = \pm 1. For q \neq \pm 1, the q-momentum is

  p_q(\beta) =  \sum_{j=1}^{k} [\epsilon_j]_q
  =  \sum_{j=1}^{k} \frac{q^{\epsilon_j} - q^{-\epsilon_j}}{q - q^{-1}},

where [\epsilon]_q = (q^{\epsilon} - q^{-\epsilon})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer.
rem:q-momentum-remark:
Remark Writhe equality, trace form and canonicity of the q-momentum. The q-momentum is the braid writhe of the canonical representative, weighted by the Hecke deformation parameter:

  p_q(\beta) = \sum_{j=1}^{k} \epsilon_j = w(\beta).

On that domain, [+1]_q = 1 and [-1]_q = -1 exactly. Each crossing contributes precisely its sign, and the q-momentum coincides with the classical writhe w(\beta) for all such q — not only in the limit q \to 1 (where the removable 0/0 singularity of [\pm 1]_q takes the same values \pm 1). The q-deformation operates trivially at single crossings; it would distinguish multi-strand contributions |\epsilon| \geq 2, but these do not occur in a braid word.

Equivalently, the q-momentum is the trace of the braid in the fundamental representation of H_n(R, q):

  p_q(\beta) =  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{fund}}(\rho(\beta))

where \rho: B_n \to H_n(R, q) is the Hecke representation.

Canonicity of the representative. The writhe is not a link invariant. Conjugation \beta \mapsto \gamma\beta\gamma^{-1} — the horizontal direction of the brane tower — preserves it, but stabilisation \beta \in B_n \mapsto \beta\sigma_n^{\pm 1} \in B_{n+1} presents the same link and shifts it by \pm 1. Both facts are proved. So p_q is a function of the braid word, and becomes a function of the particle only after the level is pinned; the framework pins it at the minimal level, where the surviving moves are horizontal. The single datum of the pair (w, n) that survives the vertical move unaided is the parity (w - n) \bmod 2, which is the component parity of the closure and carries one bit — far too little to serve as p_q.

prop:q-momentum-properties:
Proposition Additivity, Markov invariance, and parity of q-momentum. The q-momentum p_q satisfies:

  1. Additivity under concatenation: p_q(\beta_1 \beta_2) = p_q(\beta_1) + p_q(\beta_2) (because the trace is linear on the Iwahori--Hecke algebra).
  2. Invariance under Markov I: p_q is conjugation-invariant (the cyclic property of the trace).
  3. Shift under Markov II: stabilization \beta \mapsto \beta \sigma_n^{\pm 1} shifts p_q by \pm [1]_q. This is the q-analogue of adding one unit of momentum.
  4. Parity: Under the mirror \sigma: \beta \mapsto \beta^{\sigma} (reverse all crossings), p_q(\beta^{\sigma}) = -p_{q^{-1}}(\beta). Parity violation at q \neq 1 means p_q(\beta^{\sigma}) \neq -p_q(\beta).
def:q-angular-momentum:
Definition q-Angular momentum from the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Casimir. Let K = \hat{\beta} be a knot/link with braid representative \beta \in B_n. The q-angular momentum is the eigenvalue of the q-Casimir element C_q (the q-Casimir element) on the spin-j irreducible of \mathrm{SU}_q(2):

  J_q^2(K) =  [j]_q  [j+1]_q
  =  \frac{q^j - q^{-j}}{q - q^{-1}} \cdot
        \frac{q^{j+1} - q^{-(j+1)}}{q - q^{-1}}

where j is the spin quantum number that the Jones--Wenzl projector p_n acting on the n-strand braid determines: j = n/2 for the highest-weight component.
rem:q-angular-momentum-interpretation:
Remark Jones polynomial connection, building block values, and nuclear q-angular momentum. At q = 1: J_q^2 \to j(j+1), the standard Casimir.

The q-deformed angular momentum operators.

The generators J_+, J_-, J_z of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) satisfy:

  [J_z, J_{\pm}] = \pm J_{\pm}, \qquad
  [J_+, J_-] = [2 J_z]_q
  =  \frac{q^{2J_z} - q^{-2J_z}}{q - q^{-1}}

This differs from the classical [J_+, J_-] = 2J_z: 2J_z is replaced by its q-number [2J_z]_q. The raising and lowering operators do not relate by a simple conjugation.

Connection to the Jones polynomial.

The Jones polynomial J_K(q) of a knot K is the quantum trace over the spin-\tfrac{1}{2} representation:

  J_K(q) =  \mathrm{tr}_{V_{1/2}}(\rho(\beta))

The colored Jones polynomial J_K^{(j)}(q) uses the spin-j representation. The recursion between colored Jones polynomials encodes the q-angular momentum:

  J_K^{(j+1/2)}(q) =  [2j+1]_q \cdot J_K^{(j)}(q) +
  \text{(lower-order terms)}

Knot n (strands) j J_q^2 at the aether parameter q Classical j(j+1)

Nuclear q-angular momentum.

For a nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) with A = Z + N:

  J_q^2(\mathcal{N}) =  [J]_q  [J+1]_q

Here J is the ground-state spin fixed by the nuclear link's embedding in the Temperley--Lieb algebra TL_A(\delta) with \delta = -(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}).
def:q-energy:
Definition q-Deformed Energy. The q-energy of a particle knot K evaluates the categorical Hamiltonian in the dimensionless aether action/mass chart (\ell_P = \hbar_q\,t_P = 1), summing the rotational, translational, and rest-action projections derived from (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) and the aether parameter q.

Let K = \hat{\beta} be a particle knot with braid representative \beta \in B_n. The q-energy is

  \mathfrak{E}_q(K) \;=\; \underbrace{J_q^2(K) \cdot \hbar_q}_{\text{rotational}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{p_q(\beta)^2 \cdot \hbar_q / (2\,[n]_q)}_{\text{translational}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{S}_q(K)}_{\text{rest action / mass}},

where:

  • J_q^2(K) = [j]_q [j+1]_q is the q-angular momentum (q-angular momentum),
  • p_q(\beta) is the q-momentum (writhe) (q-momentum),
  • \mathfrak{S}_q(K) = \mathrm{tr}_\tau(\rho(\beta)) is the categorical action — the Markov trace of the braid in the Hecke algebra H_n(R, q),
  • \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} is the quantum Planck constant,
  • [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-number.

At rest (p_q = 0, J_q = 0):

  \mathfrak{E}_q(K)\big|_{\text{rest}} \;=\; \mathfrak{S}_q(K) \;=\; \mathfrak{m}(K)

in the aether mass chart, whereas converting to the causal-cone chart (c_q = 1/(q - 1)) rescales the rest value by c_q^2 to \mathfrak{E}(K) = \mathfrak{m}(K)\,c_q^2 = \mathfrak{m}(K)/(q - 1)^2 (categorical Hamiltonian).
rem:q-energy-terms-and-limits:
Remark The three energy terms, classical/deep-quantum limits, and crossing-energy relation. This remark unpacks the three terms of the q-energy \mathfrak{E}_q(K) in the aether action/mass chart of the categorical Hamiltonian, its classical and deep-quantum limits, and its distinction from the crossing energy.

The three terms.

  1. Rotational term J_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q: The q-deformed rotational contribution. For a spin-\frac{1}{2} state at the aether parameter q, [1/2]_q [3/2]_q \cdot \hbar_q \approx 0.818 \times 0.0991 \approx 0.0811. This vanishes at q = 1 (where \hbar_q \to 0).
  2. Translational term p_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q / (2[n]_q): The q-deformed writhe kinetic contribution, with denominator [n]_q supplying the q-deformed strand inertia.
  3. Rest-action term \mathfrak{S}_q(K): The categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q = \mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{L}_q) evaluated on the static knot (\mathcal{L}_1 = 0), which coincides with the rest projection of the categorical Hamiltonian in the aether mass chart (\ell_P = \hbar_q\,t_P = 1):
  \mathfrak{S}_q(K) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)).

At a single brane level, its magnitude equals |\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))| (categorical mass as Markov trace). Converting from the aether mass chart to the causal-cone chart multiplies by c_q^2 = 1/(q - 1)^2, while dividing the electronic causal-cone rest energy \mathfrak{m}_e c_q^2 by the Planck tick t_P = q/(q - 1) yields the per-tick hadronic scale \mathfrak{E}_0 = \mathfrak{m}_e/\bigl(q(q - 1)\bigr). For torus knots (including the trefoil), the single-level trace is nonzero whereas the hyperbolic volume vanishes; the tower mass arises from quantum dilogarithm contributions across the brane tower (mass endomorphism conjecture).

Limits.

Limit \mathfrak{E}_q(K) (aether mass chart)
q = 1 (classical) j(j+1) \cdot 0 + w^2 \cdot 0 + \mathfrak{S}_1 = \mathfrak{S}_1
q \to \infty (deep-quantum) J_q^2 \to q^{2j+1}, \; p_q \to w \cdot q, \; \mathfrak{S}_q \to \infty
Rest frame (p_q = 0, J_q = 0) \mathfrak{S}_q(K) = \mathfrak{m}(K) (rescaled to \mathfrak{m}(K)\,c_q^2 in the causal-cone chart)

Distinction from crossing energy.

Whereas \mathfrak{S}_q(K) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)) is a non-additive Markov trace invariant under braid conjugation and Reidemeister moves (up to framing), the crossing-level functional assigns q to each positive crossing and -q^{-1} to each negative crossing, with mean asymmetry \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \approx 0.1045 per crossing. Because q \neq q^{-1}, positive and negative crossings carry unequal Skein weights, providing the algebraic source of parity asymmetry before trace evaluation.
rem:noether-theorem-callout:
Remark Noether's theorem in the q-deformed setting: symmetries, conservation, and anomalies. The three q-deformed kinematic quantities—q-momentum (q-momentum), q-angular momentum (q-angular momentum), and q-energy (q-energy)—form a q-deformed Noether dictionary. Each arises from a symmetry of the categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q (categorical action) through the variational equations (variational equations), extending Noether's theorem directly.

Symmetry Generator Conserved quantity (q = 1) q-Deformed quantity Source
Time translation Reeb flow \xi_R Energy E \mathfrak{E}_q(K) Categorical action \mathfrak{S}_q
Spatial translation Braid stabilisation Momentum p p_q(\beta) (writhe) Markov II shift
Rotation \mathrm{SU}(2) action Angular momentum J^2 J_q^2 = [j]_q[j+1]_q \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Casimir
Gauge Quantum gauge group G_q Charge Coulomb charge Q(K) Tannaka–Krein reconstruction

Classical limit. At q = 1, the q-deformations collapse: \hbar_q \to 0, [n]_q \to n, and each q-quantity reduces to its classical counterpart. Noether's theorem holds exactly, and the variational equations yield the standard Einstein, Yang–Mills, and Dirac equations.

q-Anomaly. At q \neq 1, the correspondence deforms rather than breaks. The key mechanism is d_q^2 \neq 0 (non-vanishing of d_q^2): the q-differential does not square to zero. The classical chain of "symmetry \Rightarrow closed current \Rightarrow conserved charge" acquires a correction term at each step.

  1. Energy is not naively conserved in transitions. The Q-value of a nuclear decay differs from the sum of product kinetic energies by a q-anomaly \delta_q \propto \hbar_q^2. A shift in the effective aether parameter absorbs the "missing" energy. The conserved quantity is the full categorical action evaluated at the shifted q.
  2. Momentum acquires an anomalous correction \delta p_q \propto \hbar_q from the non-commutativity of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra.
  3. Angular momentum remains exactly conserved (the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Casimir commutes with the coproduct), but its eigenvalues are q-deformed: [j]_q[j+1]_q \neq j(j+1).

Noether's theorem survives the q-deformation, but the conserved quantities become categorical. They live in the Hecke algebra H_n(R, q), not in classical phase space. The archimedean (numerical) values obtained via the fibre functor \tau carry q-corrections, which manifest as measurable anomalies in precision experiments.
sec:atom-isotope-confinement-intro: This section proves existence, uniqueness, continuity, and local constancy of the shadow-price ordering off the phase-boundary variety, and concludes by deriving the zero-parameter per-component linking-weight selection rule \mathrm{lw}(c)(q) = \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda \vdash (c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda at its exact c = 1 (knot), c = 3 (Borromean link), and c = 2 (Hopf link) anchors.
def:knot-operator-energy:
Definition Knot operator energy (LP-dual shadow price). Let H_n(R, q) be the Hecke algebra at aether parameter q. For each Wedderburn block indexed by a partition \lambda \vdash k (k = 2, \ldots, k_{\max}(K, q), where k_{\max}(K, q) is the per-atom truncation determined by the interaction-strand requirement of K — see confinement level), the knot operator energy of \lambda at q is the magnitude of its Kantorovich--Fenchel LP-dual reduced cost (shadow price) relative to the attaining minimum sector of the categorical Hamiltonian in dimensionless per-irrep units:

  E(\lambda, q)
  \;:=\;
  \bigl| u_\lambda(q) \bigr|
  \;=\;
  \left|
    \frac{w_\lambda(q)}{d_\lambda(q)}
    \;-\;
    \frac{1}{[k]_q!}
  \right|,

where w_\lambda(q) = d_q(\lambda)^2 / [k]_q! is the Wedderburn weight, d_\lambda(q) = \dim_q V_\lambda is the quantum dimension, and y_0 = 1/[k]_q! = \min_\lambda\, w_\lambda/d_\lambda is the dual threshold across partitions of k, attained with zero shadow price (u_\lambda = 0) on the 1-dimensional (k) and (1^k) representations.

Values. The energy takes values in:

  • Archimedean realisation R = \mathbb{R}: E(\lambda, q) \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} (totally ordered).
  • Non-archimedean \mathbb{Q}_p: E(\lambda, q) \in \{p^{-n} : n \in \mathbb{Z}\} \cup \{0\} (totally ordered).
  • Finite field \mathbb{F}_p: no archimedean absolute value exists. The energy filtration is undefined. Confinement falls back to ILP feasibility (see stable atom), which is base-ring-independent.
rem:knot-operator-energy-vanishing:
Remark Vanishing locus and cheap/expensive operators. Vanishing locus. The set \{q \in Q : E(\lambda, q) = 0\} is the LP boundary for partition \lambda. At these q-values, the operator \lambda becomes constraint-binding. Its inclusion or exclusion in the LP-dual basis switches. Crossing such a q-value marks a categorical phase transition for any atom whose NF includes operator \lambda.

Cheap and expensive operators. The 1-dimensional partitions (k), (1^k) satisfy w_\lambda/d_\lambda = 1/[k]_q!, so E(\lambda, q) = 0 identically. These operators carry no shadow-price weight and are always available. Only mixing partitions (d_\lambda \geq 2) possess nonzero E and contribute to the confinement filtration.
rem:knot-operator-energy-consumers: Remark Consumers: gluon-channel selection by energy minimisation. The proton and neutron select gluon-stabilisation channels by minimising the knot operator energy E(\lambda, q) across partitions of H_3(q).
prop:knot-operator-energy-exists:
Proposition Existence of the knot operator energy. For any partition \lambda \vdash k with k \leq k_{\max} and any q in the generic locus \{q \in R : [k]_q! \neq 0 \;\forall k \leq k_{\max}\}, the knot operator energy E(\lambda, q) = |u_\lambda(q)| exists as an element of the absolute-value image |R| of the base ring.

Proof. The shadow price u_\lambda(q) = w_\lambda(q)/d_\lambda(q) - 1/[k]_q! \in R is a rational function of q with denominator [k]_q! \cdot d_\lambda(q). Both factors are nonzero on the generic locus, since [k]_q! \neq 0 implies [j]_q \neq 0 for every hook length j \leq k in the quantum hook-length formula for d_\lambda(q). The absolute value |\cdot|: R \to |R| is well-defined for:

  • R = \mathbb{R}: archimedean |\cdot|_\infty, image \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0};
  • R = \mathbb{Q}_p: p-adic |\cdot|_p, image \{p^{-n}\} \cup \{0\};
  • R = \mathbb{F}_p: the only absolute value is the trivial one, so there is no archimedean place. The energy filtration is undefined and confinement falls back to ILP feasibility (stable atom).

In each archimedean or non-archimedean case, E(\lambda, q) exists and is uniquely determined by \lambda and q.
prop:knot-operator-energy-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of the knot operator energy. The knot operator energy E(\lambda, q) = |u_\lambda(q)| (knot operator energy) is uniquely determined by:

  1. the partition \lambda \vdash k (a classical Young diagram — q-independent indexing),
  2. the aether parameter q in the generic locus,
  3. the choice of absolute value |\cdot|_v on R (archimedean or non-archimedean).

Uniqueness holds "up to base ring equivalence": the same shadow price evaluated under equivalent absolute values yields equal energies.

Proof. The shadow price u_\lambda(q) is unique in R by LP duality (complementary slackness dictates a unique dual variable per binding constraint). The absolute value |\cdot|_v is unique up to equivalence within each place by Ostrowski's theorem (over \mathbb{Q}). For R \in \{\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{Q}_p, \mathbb{F}_p\}, the base ring itself fixes the canonical choice.
def:local-shadow-ordering:
Definition Local shadow-price ordering \preceq_q. For two partitions \lambda_1, \lambda_2 with shadow prices y_{\lambda_1}(q), y_{\lambda_2}(q) \in R, the local shadow-price ordering at q is:

  \lambda_1 \;\preceq_q\; \lambda_2
  \;\iff\;
  \exists\, U \ni q\;\text{open such that}\;
  |y_{\lambda_1}(q')| \;\leq\; |y_{\lambda_2}(q')|
  \;\;\forall q' \in U.

This reads: "\lambda_1 has at most the energy of \lambda_2 on a neighborhood of q".
prop:shadow-price-continuity:
Proposition Continuity of shadow prices on the generic locus. Each shadow price u_\lambda(q) = w_\lambda(q)/d_\lambda(q) - 1/[k]_q! is a rational function of q over the base ring, with denominator [k]_q! \cdot d_\lambda(q). On the generic locus \{q : [k]_q! \cdot d_\lambda(q) \neq 0\}, u_\lambda is continuous in q (smooth in the \mathbb{R} realisation, p-adic continuous in \mathbb{Q}_p, well-defined Zariski on \mathbb{F}_p).

By continuity, if |y_{\lambda_1}(q)| < |y_{\lambda_2}(q)| strictly, then the local shadow-price ordering \lambda_1 \preceq_q \lambda_2 holds on a neighborhood.
prop:phase-boundary-variety:
Proposition Phase-boundary variety \mathcal{B} is Zariski-closed and measure-zero. The locus

  \mathcal{B}_{\lambda_1, \lambda_2}
  \;:=\;
  \{q \in Q : |y_{\lambda_1}(q)| = |y_{\lambda_2}(q)|\}

is a Zariski-closed subvariety of Q, generically of codimension \geq 1 (defined by the polynomial equation y_{\lambda_1}^2(q) = y_{\lambda_2}^2(q)). The full phase-boundary variety is

  \mathcal{B}
  \;:=\;
  \bigcup_{\lambda_1 \neq \lambda_2}
    \mathcal{B}_{\lambda_1, \lambda_2}
  \;\cup\;
  \bigcup_\lambda
    \{q : u_\lambda(q) = 0\}.

This is the union of pairwise-equality varieties and shadow-price-vanishing varieties. \mathcal{B} has measure zero in Q.
prop:confinement-local-constancy: Proposition Local constancy of confinement level off \mathcal{B}. The confinement level \ell(K, q) is locally constant on Q \setminus \mathcal{B}. For any q \notin \mathcal{B}, there exists an open U \ni q such that \ell(K, q') = \ell(K, q) for all q' \in U. The level changes only at points of the phase-boundary variety \mathcal{B} — these correspond exactly to the categorical phase boundaries.
rem:shadow-ordering-compute-shortcut: Remark Computational shortcut from local constancy. Following the unstable-atom "Computational shortcut", restrict expensive computations (per-generator \hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}} extraction) to exact evaluation only at points of the phase-boundary variety \mathcal{B}. In the complement Q \setminus \mathcal{B}, all shadow prices, the filtration, and the per-generator data are locally constant (by local constancy of confinement). Linear interpolation between nearest magic-number anchors is mathematically justified.
prop:selection-rule-anchors-c1-c3:
Proposition Per-component selection rule \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda at c=1, c=3. Let q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} and let h := q - q^{-1}. The per-component selection rule

  \mathrm{lw}(c)(q) \;:=\; \frac{1}{c+1} \sum_{\lambda \vdash (c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda

satisfies the two exact identities:

  \mathrm{lw}(1)(q) \;=\; 1 \qquad (\text{exactly, } \forall q > 0),
  \mathrm{lw}(3)(q) \;=\; \frac{3q^2 + 4 + 3q^{-2}}{4} \;=\; \frac{5}{2} + \frac{3}{4} h^2.

These form the muon (c=1, knot) and the proton (c=3, Borromean 3-link) anchors of the per-component selection rule.

Significance

The zero-parameter selection rule reads \mathrm{lw}(L) = \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash(c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda, where c is the number of link components. The c=1 case equals 1 for all q (muon, a single-component knot with \mathrm{lw} = 1), and the c=3 case equals the Family-A formula \frac{5}{2} + \frac{3}{4}h^2 (proton, a three-component Borromean link). This proposition derives both identities directly from the hook-length formula: the sums run over the partitions of 2 and 4, and each \dim_q V_\lambda is [n]_q! divided by the product of the hook q-integers of \lambda.

Proof structure

The proof consists of two purely algebraic identities at the symbolic level:

  1. c=1 anchor: \frac{1}{2}\bigl( \dim_q V_{(2)} + \dim_q V_{(1,1)} \bigr) = 1. Both q-dimensions equal 1 (each partition of 2 has a hook product equal to the q-factorial), so the average is exactly 1.

  2. c=3 anchor: \frac{1}{4} \bigl( \dim_q V_{(4)} + \dim_q V_{(3,1)} + \dim_q V_{(2,2)} + \dim_q V_{(2,1,1)} + \dim_q V_{(1,1,1,1)} \bigr) = (3q^2 + 4 + 3q^{-2})/4.

    Using the explicit q-hook formula:

    • \dim_q V_{(4)} = \dim_q V_{(1,1,1,1)} = 1
    • \dim_q V_{(3,1)} = \dim_q V_{(2,1,1)} = [3]_q = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}
    • \dim_q V_{(2,2)} = [4]_q / [2]_q = q^2 + q^{-2}

    Their sum is 1 + (q^2{+}1{+}q^{-2}) + (q^2{+}q^{-2}) + (q^2{+}1{+}q^{-2}) + 1 = 4 + 3q^2 + 3q^{-2}. Dividing by 4 yields the stated form. The h^2 form follows from q^2 + q^{-2} = h^2 + 2.

    Both steps operate as pure polynomial identities in \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. They hold once the q^{-1} denominators are cleared.

q-usage discipline

This holds over real q > 0 (the aether-anchor regime). Both identities are q-rational, fibre-level constructs. The c=1 case holds for ALL q > 0 (an infinite set of constraints, not a single point).

Cross-references

  • Coulomb charge of a knot composite — introduces the h = q - q^{-1} structure at the per-crossing level.
  • Coulomb/strong ratio \tanh(\ln q) is the q-rational (q^2-1)/(q^2+1) — companion identity proving \tanh(\ln q) = (q^2-1)/(q^2+1) over real q > 0.
prop:selection-rule-c2-prediction:
Proposition Per-component selection rule at c=2: \mathrm{lw}(2) = (q+1)^2/(3q). Let q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}. The per-component selection rule (Per-component selection rule \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda at c=1, c=3) applied at c=2 yields the closed form:

  \mathrm{lw}(2)(q) \;:=\; \frac{1}{3} \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3} \dim_q V_\lambda
  \;=\; \frac{2 + [2]_q}{3} \;=\; \frac{(q+1)^2}{3q}.

This supplies the rule's prediction for a 2-component link (e.g. the Hopf link). The closed form is a finite Laurent rational over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. Like the c=1 and c=3 anchors, it is derivation-tight (no fit, zero free parameters).

Significance

The per-component rule states \mathrm{lw}(c) = (1/(c+1)) \sum_{\lambda \vdash (c+1)} \dim_q V_\lambda. It is anchored at c=1 (muon, \mathrm{lw}=1 exactly \forall q) and c=3 (proton, \mathrm{lw} = 5/2 + (3/4)h^2 via Family-A). The c=2 case provides the first testable prediction of the rule beyond the two known anchors.

This proposition derives the closed form for c=2 from the hook-length formula itself: the sum runs over the three partitions of 3, with \dim_q V_{(2,1)} = [2]_q derived from the hook multiset \{3,1,1\} rather than asserted. Its anchors are derived the same way. Any independent determination of a 2-component link's linking_weight—such as a Hopf-link or gluon EM-linking application—can be tested against this exact formula.

Proof structure

The proof rests on a single algebraic identity at the symbolic level:

  \frac{1}{3} \bigl( \dim_q V_{(3)} + \dim_q V_{(2,1)} + \dim_q V_{(1,1,1)} \bigr)
  \;=\; \frac{(q+1)^2}{3q}.

Using the explicit q-hook values for partitions of 3:

  • \dim_q V_{(3)} = 1 (single-row Young diagram, all hooks contribute trivially)
  • \dim_q V_{(2,1)} = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} (standard rep at H_3; q-hook computation)
  • \dim_q V_{(1,1,1)} = 1 (single-column, conjugate of V_{(3)})

Their sum is 2 + q + q^{-1}. Dividing by 3 yields (2 + q + q^{-1})/3 = (q^2 + 2q + 1)/(3q) = (q+1)^2/(3q).

This constitutes a pure polynomial-ring identity over \mathbb{R}_{>0} once the q^{-1} denominators are cleared.

q-usage discipline

This holds over real q > 0 (aether-anchor regime). The closed form (q+1)^2/(3q) is a Laurent rational in \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] — a fibre-level construction. At q = q_0, it evaluates to \approx 1.337. There is no |q|=1 step; both q and q^{-1} are real positive at any real q > 0.

Cross-references

  • Per-component selection rule \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda\vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda at c=1, c=3 — the two known anchors that establish the rule's existence.
sec:braiding-relations-intro: The categorical axioms of a quantum observable universe impose polynomial relations on the Iwahori–Hecke generators beyond the bare braid and quadratic relations, acting as a cohomological spectral filter on candidate closed braids.
